etymologies.etymologyHTML: From earlier peake, peek, peke, from Middle English pek (in place names), itself an alteration of pike, pyke, pyk (“a sharp point, pike”), from Old English pīc, piic (“a pike, needle, pin, peak, pinnacle”), from Proto-Germanic *pīkaz (“peak”). Cognate with Dutch piek (“pike, point, summit, peak”), Danish pik (“pike, peak”), Swedish pik (“pike, lance, point, peak”), Norwegian pik (“peak, summit”). More at pike.

definitions.definition: A point; the sharp end or top of anything that terminates in a point; as, the peak, or front, of a cap.

quote.citation: 2002, Joy of Cooking: All About Cookies, →ISBN, page 29:
quote.text: A less risky method is to lift your whisk or beater to check the condition of the peaks of the egg whites; the foam should be just stiff enough to stand up in well-defined, unwavering peaks.

definitions.definition: The highest value reached by some quantity in a time period.

quote.citation: 2012 October 23, David Leonhardt, New York Times, retrieved 24 October 2012:
quote.text: By last year, family income was 8 percent lower than it had been 11 years earlier, at its peak in 2000, according to inflation-adjusted numbers from the Census Bureau.

definitions.definition: (geography) The top, or one of the tops, of a hill, mountain, or range, ending in a point.
(geography) The whole hill or mountain, especially when isolated.

quote.citation: 1898, Arnold Henry Savage Landor, chapter 62, in In the Forbidden Land:
quote.text: To the South we observed a large plain some ten miles wide, with snowy peaks rising on the farther side. In front was a hill projecting into the plain, on which stood a mani wall; and this latter discovery made me feel quite confident that I was on the high road to Lhassa.

definitions.definition: (clothing, UK) visor (horizontal part of a cap sticking out in front and shading the wearer's eyes)
(nautical) The upper aftermost corner of a fore-and-aft sail.
(nautical) The narrow part of a vessel's bow, or the hold within it.
(nautical) The extremity of an anchor fluke; the bill.
(mathematics) A local maximum of a function, e.g. for sine waves, each point at which the value of y is at its maximum.
(transitive, nautical) To raise the point of (a gaff) closer to perpendicular.
(transitive, signal processing) To exceed the maximum signal amplitude of (a piece of equipment), resulting in clipping of the signal.

quote.citation: 2023 September 22, HarryBlank, “Off Track”, in SCP Foundation‎[1], archived from the original on 25 May 2024:
quote.text: "Dr. Reynders?" Udo prodded."Yes!" the woman shouted, peaking the speakers with a screech. "Of course I am! What the hell else could this be?! Of course I'm seeing double! And hearing double! AND THINKING DOUBLE! AND I'M DOING THE BEST I CAN WITH IT, BUT IT'S GETTING TO BE JUST A LITTLE BIT MUCH!" Her voice grew increasingly hoarse as it grew in volume, finally cracking on the last word.

definitions.definition: To reach a highest degree or maximum.
To rise or extend into a peak or point; to form, or appear as, a peak.

quote.citation: 1659, T[itus] Livius [i.e., Livy], “(please specify the book number)”, in Philemon Holland, transl., The Romane Historie […], London:  […]  W. Hunt, for George Sawbridge, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: There peaketh up a mightie high mounte.

definitions.definition: (intransitive)
(gender-critical) To cause to adopt gender-critical or trans-exclusionary views (ellipsis of peak trans).

quote.text: I came to this via sport but the thing that really peaked me was this.
My friend peaked me last year, at the GRA [Gender Recognition Act] consultation.
Solidarity from Spain, @jk_rowling. Thank you for peaking so many people all over the world.

definitions.definition: At the greatest extent; maximum.
(slang) Maximal, quintessential, archetypical; representing the culmination of its type.
(MLE) Bad.

quote.citation: 2015, “Its Peak”, performed by Tinie Tempah (featuring Stormzy and Bugzy Malone):
quote.text: When they're tryna get the girl to the crib and she leaves, it's peak / Tryna keep it discreet and she tweets, it's peak / See me rolling with 20 man deep, it's peak / Yo rudeboy, pull up, repeat, it's peak

quote.citation: 2023, Nathan Bryon, Tom Melia, directed by Raine Allen-Miller, Rye Lane, spoken by Dom (David Jonsson):
quote.text: Tempting, but I think it's actually something I need to do. Like, I get what they did was peak, but I have to take some responsibility, you know?

definitions.definition: (MLE) Unlucky; unfortunate.
(Internet slang) Very good or high-quality.
(intransitive) To become sick or wan.
(intransitive) To acquire sharpness of figure or features; hence, to look thin or sickly.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To pry; to peep slyly.
Alternative form of peag (“wampum”).
